summary: Introductory security posture and deployment options discovery. Customer is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem). Primary concerns: KMS/HSM integration, audit log retention and access controls, SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping, SOC2/ISO evidence, and data residency/retention for regulated datasets.
topics: RBAC and least privilege for internal teams
Audit logs: retention, access, and export
Encryption keys: customer-managed KMS / HSM options
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-10 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (CTO, Skyward), Priya Rao (Head of InfoSec, Skyward), Daniel Kim (Platform Engineer, Skyward)

00:00 Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off, um quick agenda — security posture, deployment fit, and next steps.
00:18 Alex Moreno: yeah thanks jordan, we want to understand what we would actually need to do to run redwood either hosted or private. our compliance team is pushing for customer-managed keys for some datasets.
00:30 Maya Singh: perfect, we'll cover KMS and HSM options. quick note — redwood is SOC2 Type II and we also maintain an iso27001 program, we can share the summary.
00:45 Priya Rao: can you clarify "maintain" — do you have the certificate and latest report? our procurement needs the report and the SOC2 cover letter.
00:58 Jordan Park: yes, we have a SOC2 report, and an iso 27001 cert, i'll send the redacted copies. i'll include the SOC2 cover letter.
01:12 Daniel Kim: for the private option — we're particularly interested in the network topology. will redwood provide the control plane in our VPC or is that fully customer-managed?
01:28 Maya Singh: great question. for Redwood Private we offer a customer-managed control plane option where the control plane sits in your VPC — you manage ingress rules and we ship an appliance/controller. alternatively, we can do a vetted on-prem package. There are tradeoffs: the hosted control plane is fastest to set up but uses redwood-managed KMS unless you opt for dedicated private KMS integration.
01:55 Priya Rao: ok, on KMS — do you support AWS KMS customer-managed CMKs and HSM-backed keys? we require HSM-backed keys for one of our regulated datasets.
02:08 Maya Singh: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS and can support HSM-backed keys via CloudHSM for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, we have an option to configure a customer KMS per tenant via cross-account key policies. the key material does not leave the provider. there are some operational caveats around key rotation windows we'd document.
02:30 Alex Moreno: rotation windows — can you give an example?
02:34 Maya Singh: for the hosted cross-account KMS setup, there is a short maintenance window for rotating keys where we rewrap token material. usually we recommend quarterly rotation but we can do more frequent rotations, might impact short-term request throughput during the rotation handshake — small spike in latency.
02:55 Daniel Kim: hmm ok that might be fine. what about encryption in transit? we need TLS 1.2+ and mTLS between services for private deployment.
03:06 Maya Singh: all traffic is TLS 1.2+, we support TLS1.3. for private deployments we can enable mTLS for internal service-to-service. we also support customer-provided certs when running in your VPC.
03:20 Priya Rao: audit logs: retention and who can access them? we need to retain immutable audit logs for 2 years and ensure only our SecOps can view exportable logs.
03:33 Jordan Park: audit logs are shipped to a customer-owned storage endpoint for Private, and for Dedicated we can configure S3 export to your bucket with server-side encryption using your KMS keys. For Hosted, we provide log exports via a push to a customer webhook or s3 — access controls can be restricted through IAM roles and we support role-based export permissions.
03:58 Maya Singh: one caveat — hosted logs are retained in our analytics for 30 days by default for observability, but exports to your bucket are immediate and you can configure retention there.
04:12 Alex Moreno: do you have fine-grained RBAC for Red team vs SRE vs app owners? we want least privilege and audit trails for admin actions.
04:22 Maya Singh: yes, we have RBAC tied to SSO via SAML and SCIM. you can map groups to roles (read-only, developer, admin, secops). we log role changes and admin actions. for Dedicated and Private you can also use your IdP to govern sessions and token lifetimes.
04:40 Priya Rao: is session recording or user activity trace available for compliance?
04:45 Maya Singh: we emit audit events for all API operations and admin console actions — these can be streamed to your SIEM. we don't capture full session video but we do capture the command + metadata.
04:58 Daniel Kim: any limits on audit event retention size or export frequency?
05:03 Maya Singh: for exports to S3 it's effectively unlimited, retention controlled by your lifecycle rules. for hosted analytics internal retention is 30 days; we have an add-on for extended retention if you need us to hold it longer for a fee.
05:20 Alex Moreno: ok, let's talk about data residency. some of our clients require EU-only processing. can Redwood route requests to specific regions?
05:32 Jordan Park: yes, we support region routing and have EU-hosted regions for data processing. for Dedicated and Private we can guarantee processing in selected regions. for hosted we also support a data region setting per project to keep inference in region.
05:46 Priya Rao: legal/regulatory: do you support data deletion requests and can you provide proof of deletion?
05:53 Maya Singh: yes, we support per-customer deletion requests. for Private, you control deletion. for Hosted, we have a documented process and can provide deletion certificates showing artifacts removed from our stores and caches, and we scrub prefix caches — though we advise using client-side filtering for highly sensitive PII.
06:15 Alex Moreno: what's your stance on model caching and KV cache? could PII be inadvertently cached in prompt prefixes?
06:24 Maya Singh: we do automatic prefix and KV caching for latency. customers can opt-out of caching per route or use encrypted caching that uses customer keys, but you should design prompts to avoid returning PII; we also have tokenization and redaction hooks. this is a common area to define in the evals and we can run prompt-level regressions.
06:48 Daniel Kim: performance — for dedicated GPUs, what's typical 8k-token latency?
06:55 Maya Singh: depends on model size and quantization. a ballpark: mid-sized open models on a dedicated p4d-type pool deliver 400-800ms per 1k tokens after warm KV; large context will scale linearly. we'll put exact numbers in the benchmarking doc.
07:12 Alex Moreno: great. procurement will ask: what do you require from our side for a private deployment?
07:20 Jordan Park: short list: network peering/VPN details, a small set of service accounts, KMS key ARN if using customer-managed keys, and an SSO/SAML metadata file for IdP integration. we'll provide a runbook and an architecture diagram.
07:37 Priya Rao: SSO — SAML vs OIDC; we run Okta and Azure AD. is SAML supported and do you support SCIM user provisioning?
07:46 Maya Singh: we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC. SCIM provisioning is supported for user/group sync. for Dedicated/Private you can lock provisioning to your SCIM endpoint.
07:58 Daniel Kim: about RBAC mapping — can we map LDAP groups to roles dynamically?
08:04 Maya Singh: yes via SCIM group sync we map to roles, or you can use SAML assertions to convey role claims. we recommend using SCIM for automated provisioning.
08:15 Alex Moreno: any SOC2 control that is typically a gap for customers when onboarding?
08:20 Jordan Park: usually customers ask about data deletion evidence and key separation. we provide controls for encryption, but integration with customer KMS requires some network and IAM setup which we walk through in onboarding.
08:33 Priya Rao: ok on metrics — we want to measure request-level latency and cost per 1k tokens to compare with our in-house inference. can you provide token-level breakdowns?
08:44 Maya Singh: yes our console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. we can also set up tracing hooks to export into your telemetry.
08:56 Jordan Park: quick interjection — any blocker for doing a short POC?
09:01 Alex Moreno: the blockers are: getting SOC2 report, ensuring HSM-backed KMS integration for regulated data, and a clear ingestion/retention policy. if those look good, procurement will sign a pilot.
09:12 Jordan Park: understood. i'll send SOC2 and iso docs and a network topology doc after this call.
09:20 Priya Rao: on logging access — who at redwood can see customer logs? need to ensure only a small ops team with emergency access can view logs and there's an approval workflow.
09:31 Maya Singh: we limit raw log access to a small redwood ops squad; access is audited and requires a ticket and justification in enterprise accounts. we can also disable redwood-side console access for your org and require all troubleshooting via exported logs.
09:50 Daniel Kim: about SLA — do you provide uptime SLA for Dedicated?
09:55 Jordan Park: yes Dedicated includes an SLA. Private on-prem deployments are supported with a professional services SLA; hosted has a tiered uptime promise based on plan. we'll include SLA language in the contract stub.
10:08 Alex Moreno: last thing — can we run a quick connectivity test or smoke benchmark before a pilot kickoff?
10:16 Maya Singh: absolutely. we can provide a lightweight benchmark script that hits a small model for latency measurements and a network connectivity checklist. we'll run that with you during the deep dive.
10:26 Jordan Park: ok, recap and next steps: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs and the security whitepaper; maya will schedule the dedicated vs private deep dive and benchmark; daniel will provide retention categories and network contacts. any other asks?
10:40 Priya Rao: please also include a sample deletion certificate/template and examples of audit exports.
10:46 Jordan Park: will do.
10:50 Alex Moreno: thanks all, good call.

Notes/links shared during call:
- Security whitepaper (link): https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper (shared)
- SOC2 summary (will be emailed)
- Draft network diagram template: https://redwood.example.com/network-template (shared)

End of call.
